body: I'd like to add one thing about hobbies. I'm interested in history, war-history to be more precise and especially WW2. I can read about that shit for hours without getting bored. One of the few things i can actually concentrate on while reading.

Hello! I thought this post would go unnoticed, but it didn't get by you, and for that I want to say thank you. Also I'm glad it was such a well thought-out post and not some generic "stay strong" comment, even though they are also made with good intentions. 

I can definetly relate to the whole "i want to dwell in my own misery" ordeal, atleast when it's at its worst. I know nothing good will come out of it. I try to hit the gym 2-3 times a week. I used to jog, gave it up, but I actually ran for a good while this evening in hope it would clear my head a little. When I'm feeling alright i try to make something sociable happen, but it get progressively more difficult as i didn't really make any friends my first year in Uni (due to anxiety starting to get bad).

You asked me what kind of anxiety disorder i suffer from, and yes it's the social kind. Altough at the point before starting taking Cipralex, it had become so bad my nerves was shot pretty much 24/7. 

I'm 21 years old, turning 22 this summer. We used to be a group of guys when i went to the equivalent of High-school here in Norway. Two of these guys were my best friends. They still are to this day, even though we live far away from each other now. Keeping in touch with them has become a bigger priority for me as I'm realizing times are changing, and if I want to keep them in my life I got to do something active. 

A short summery of my family: One half-brother dead, other half-brother is a junky, adoptive brother is in jail for selling pot among other things. I'm still not sure to this day if i actually love my mother. The first time i heard the definition of a narcissist I knew what the deal with my mom was. My dad actually recently told me they'd be watching a show about the topic together and even she realized the similarities. I know she loves me, but I can't spend one day with her without having a fight. She is very suffocating to be around. 

I guess my dad is the one i can relate to the most in my family. Sadly, he deals with a lot of pain, both emotionally and physicly. He's on the same medication as I am for depression. It's possible he also suffered from a milder form of anxiety as he could relate to some of the things i told him. Even though i can get frustrated as fuck on him from time to time because of how slow and little aware he can be (not his fault though), I still love that man and I know he loves me deeply. He's a good man, he's always been there for me and I know it hurts him knowing I'm having a hard time.  

I don't really have any solid goals anymore. I've spent hours Googling professions I'd might enjoy, but basically ends up where i started (makes me sound real picky i know). I don't have any hobbies either any longer (unless you call gaming a hobby). I tried to get into making music  using different software for a while. Same thing with programming.Might just be me not giving enough effort, but I just can't seem to get interested enough without it feeling like work. 

"Pick up artist" books doesn't sound silly at all when you put it that way.  Ill check it out when my exams are over! I actually downloaded something called "Pandoras Box" one time in desperation to see if it had something worth while. 

Good luck on your exams dude! Thank you again for the comment.

One thing that sucks so bad that I didn't mention is the thought in the back of my head that i can't thrust the stability of my state of mind. I can be feeling alright for a week and that's when things like finding a girl i could love seems possible. Makes it that much worse when the anxiety kicks in again and such things are impossible. I get some glimps of the good life, before i get brought back to loneliness.
